correctness.rationale: The theorem is correct. The frozen proof overstates the boundary translation: t'=16 can make a translated interval exceed the finite prefix if its right offset is positive. Restricting to t'=1,...,15 leaves all offsets of absolute value <q valid and the four parity/bit classes have sizes 3,4,4,4, so the claimed lower bound on repetitions follows unchanged. The same restriction handles unaligned length-(q+1) factors. Independently regenerated all 36 length-nine templates and verified their disjoint start residue sets; even-index decimation then proves the all-k alignment induction. In the 15 aligned starts the triple classes give singleton indices 11 and 12 only. Direct exhaustive counting verifies k=2, including the 60 length-five starts, and corroborates n=7..10. Replay: python3 /workspace/replay/finite_checks.py. The scientific rejection below is not a rejection of the statement's truth.
